reference_resolution.rule: token_name must resolve to an actual entry in the design-tokens JSON file — no orphan references (issue-515 invariant 2).

recomputation.rule: value is recomputed by re-validating token_name's entry against the DTCG format spec, never a standalone asserted field.
recomputation.checked_by: TBD (follow-up — issue-521 out-of-scope note: per-role recomputation enforcement is a follow-up once evidence from real usage shows which roles need it)

use_when.board_condition: a new design token is proposed on the branch AND no brand-design record exists yet for that token_name

need_detector.condition: the target project has UI source files (path_patterns: **/*.tsx, **/*.jsx, **/*.vue, **/*.svelte) AND no design-tokens/*.json file exists anywhere in the repo tree
need_detector.false_positive_bound: a backend-only or CLI-only target project has no UI source files at all, so the detector never fires — zero UI surface -> silent, unconditionally

outcome_mission: the target project has an applied, consistent visual identity a user or another contributor can see and reuse — not a description of one.

mission_deliverables.fit_criterion: every token resolves to a real DTCG entry and covers at minimum color + fontFamily + fontWeight categories (reuses the spec's own reference_resolution rule)
states a numeric clear-space value and minimum size, and shows at least one correct and one incorrect usage example — not description-only

mission_deliverables.artifact: component theming: token consumption wired into at least one real UI component's stylesheet/theme file
mission_deliverables.fit_criterion: a component in the target project's source resolves a token from (1) at build/render time, checkable the same way ux-engineering's reference_resolution already checks token_name -> consuming_component

verified_by: ux-engineering — brand-design never grades its own mission_deliverables (deliverable 3 is a UX-engineering consumption point by definition; deliverables 1-2 are checked by the same role since it already reads brand-design's token file as an input to its own reference_resolution rule)
